description:
Returns the configuration decisions still pending for a new app, from the same decision map the Neblla dashboard wizard uses. Pass the `decisions` already known; the tool returns every pending decision with a description and flags: `how_to_infer` says whether it can be settled from context and `ask_user` whether it needs the developer's input; `ask_user_questions` lists the ones that do. When `have_enough_context` is true, the returned `decisions` are the input of neblla_create_app({ name, decisions }), which scaffolds the matching pattern and themed UI pieces and writes the app config. `plan` previews what that builds. Changes nothing. 

Decision ids: kind (game|app), players (single|lobby-only|multi — single = one device; lobby-only = everyone in one shared space with no separate rooms; multi = separate rooms, born with one room example: the server sets the state, the clients paint it and talk through message; a referee, a big screen with phones as pads or everyone drawing at once are recipes in neblla_get_llms({ section: "salas" })), board and master (multi only: a shared display screen, someone who leads the session; each adds its example piece), modules (the list of neblla.* modules the app carries beyond auth and db, always on, and the multiplayer ones players sets: any of social, shop, inbox, ai, api, anticheat, groups, community, business, tools, or [] — each option says what it does, what it needs and what it costs), connections (all|p2p|server), roomsPolicy (ephemeral|public|private|mixed), matchmakingMode (nocode|custom), aiPayer (off|browser|server; when ai is in modules), palette ({primary, secondary, alert} hex colors), typography (modern|editorial|techy|serif|playful).

decisions.description: Decisions answered so far, keyed by decision id. Example: { kind: "game", players: "multi", modules: ["social", "anticheat"], palette: { primary: "#0F7BD7", secondary: "#15C2B0", alert: "#FF8552" }, typography: "techy" }. Decisions already known.
